what: Before/after visual attribution for Task 28.5B: the OLD accepted reconstruction (2026-08-25) and the NEW hardened reconstruction (2026-08-30) each diffed against the SAME live-original capture from the 2026-08-30 QA session.
comparability: SAME_REFERENCE_COMPARABLE between old and new diffs; old clone built from 2026-08-25 source (drift caveat)
comparabilityDetail: SAME_REFERENCE_COMPARABLE between old and new diffs: both sides are diffed against the IDENTICAL live-original PNG bytes captured in the 2026-08-30T15-57-54-926Z QA session, so the reference is held fixed and old-vs-new channel deltas are attributable to the clone. CAVEAT: the old clone was generated from the 2026-08-25 observation/site-spec source, five days older than the reference capture, so any real linear.app drift in that window is charged to the old clone. The comparison therefore DISADVANTAGES the old build; improvements it shows are a lower bound, and any place where the old build wins is not explainable by drift.

namingConvention.source-<route>-<width>.png: the shared reference: QA live-original full-page capture (identical bytes for both diffs)
namingConvention.old-clone-<route>-<width>.png: OLD reconstruction served and captured now with the project's own QA capture path
namingConvention.new-clone-<route>-<width>.png: NEW reconstruction clone capture, copied verbatim from the QA run
namingConvention.old-diff-<route>-<width>.png: source vs old clone, current screenshot-diff module
namingConvention.new-diff-<route>-<width>.png: source vs new clone, copied verbatim from the QA run's diffs

readingTheNumbers: No single channel is the verdict. @1 counts any 1/255 change and is dominated by sub-perceptual noise; @16 gates on amplitude; dE76>2.3 is the perceptual JND and dE76>10 is clearly visible side by side. Judge visible regression on @16 and dE76>10.
